hints: A common divisor cannot exceed the smaller of the two numbers.
Build frequency counts, then try candidate divisors from largest down.
For a candidate d, count how many inputs are multiples of d; at least two means d divides a pair.
analogy: Search from large to small for a number that appears as a divisor of at least two inputs.
example: If values 3,6,9 occur, 3 divides all three, so it is a common divisor of a pair.
algorithm: Count occurrences of each value. For d descending from maxA, sum frequencies at d,2d,3d,...; print the first d whose multiple count is at least 2.
correctness: If at least two array entries are multiples of d, d is their common divisor; descending order ensures the first valid candidate is largest.
complexity: O(M log M) time and O(M) space.
